open_points.subject: scope and cardinality of clock readings
open_points.text: A28 says “one wall reading per request” and “one reading per request” of the elapsed clock, while `system_clock` says “One wall reading per call” and “one elapsed reading per call”; A28 also says an operation reads once and `audit_writer` takes its own reading when appending. No request-scoped clock context or cache is owned, and `system_clock` expressly hides no cache.
open_points.question: Does “request” mean one HTTP request, one use-case operation, or one invocation of `utc_now`/`monotonic_seconds`; specifically, may authorization, the owning use case, and `audit_writer` take separate wall readings during one HTTP request?
options: Exactly one wall reading for the whole HTTP request, shared by authorization, the use case and audit append
One wall reading per use-case operation, with `audit_writer` taking the stated separate reading
One host-clock read per call to `system_clock`, allowing every consumer call to receive a different value
open_points.default_guess: Treat the rule as one reading per use-case operation, with the explicit separate `audit_writer` reading; interpret “per request” as an imprecise reference to a clock call.

witness.initial: An active staff session submits one authorized mutation that writes a business record and an audit record.
events: `authorization_guard` validates session expiry and asks `system_clock` for the current wall time.
The owning use-case module asks `system_clock` for the mutation timestamp.
`audit_writer` appends the audit record and asks `system_clock` for `occurred_at`.
outcomes: A request-wide interpretation permits one host-clock read, so authorization, the business write and the audit append reuse one instant.
The operation/per-call interpretation permits three readings; the business timestamp can differ from the authorization instant and the audit timestamp can differ from both.
witness.observer: A verification check instrumenting `system_clock`, and an administrator reading the persisted business and audit timestamps, see the difference.
